payload.text: Binary Solution: Deconstructing the LSAT since 1991 - Overview Binary Solution: Deconstructing the LSAT since 1991 HOME MISSION SCHEDULES & REGISTRATION INSTRUCTOR COURSE MATERIALS WHY IT WORKS LSAT DATES &POLICIES LSAC POLICIES CHOOSING AN LSAT CONTACT CLICK HERE FOR COURSE ​ SCHEDULES ​ & REGISTRATION Binary Solution is a unique system for solving the LSAT that is simple enough to be mastered by anyone and powerful enough to raise LSAT scores by an average of 12-15 points-- while also providing students with an advantage in law school* ​﻿﻿﻿"Binary thinking involves exercising the 'left brain,' the analytical part of the mind that governs much of legal reasoning... improving left-brain skills and the speed at which they are performed leads to improvements in LSAT scores, as well as improved performance on law school exams and on the bar exam." -Mary Lu Bilek, Former Dean of CUNY School of Law A Solution Based on Science The Binary Solution is based on a logical deconstruction of the LSAT-- a process that reduces the exam to its smallest quanta of information. Our deconstruction has revealed that the quantum of intellectual currency on the LSAT is the issue , because issues give rise to questions, both on the LSAT and in the Law. Our unique theoretical lens treats every LSAT question as a weighted sum of issues , and since this approach is granular, students are prepared for any juxtaposition of issues that may appear on the LSAT. "The Binary Algorithm is exactly how one would program a computer to solve the test" -Eben Moglen, Columbia Law School Professor & Founding Director, Software Freedom Law Center The LSAT Measures Binary Thinking To facilitate issue-spotting, we have isolated the exam's critical semantic binary operators : i.e., words that appear in every LSAT question and that function to trigger the issues that are relevant to the solution of any LSAT question. By focusing on the binary operators (such as if, but , and, or ), our students develop a semantic net for spotting the language that triggers the answer to any LSAT question. Since this semantic approach operates on the level of the word, our students do not need to classify the entire exercise before solving it-- they begin to solve from the moment they start reading each LSAT question . Naturally, this efficient approach reduces solution time. ​ "Binary Solution taught me a whole new appreciation for the LSAT" - Anna Ivey, Esq., Former Dean of Admissions at University of Chicago Law School & Author of the Ivey Guide to Law School Admissions Major Law Schools Endorse Our Approach Longitudinal studies conducted by Law School faculty have confirmed that our program increases LSAT scores. Due to its rigorous content, several law schools even recommend Binary Solution as a primer for entering law students. Our intensive program is designed to produce scores in the 160 to 180 range. Consequently, our students typically get admitted to top-tier law schools.
